description: Experience the rich, creamy indulgence of classic Butter Chicken, a beloved Indian delicacy known as Murgh Makhani. This authentic recipe features tender chicken pieces simmered in a luscious tomato-based gravy, enriched with butter and cream. It is a harmonious blend of sweet, tangy, and subtly spicy flavors, perfect for a comforting meal.

ingredients.item: Boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts

instructions.title: Marinate the Chicken
instructions.text: In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with yogurt, 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste, 1 tsp red chili powder, 1/2 tsp turmeric powder, 1/2 tsp garam masala, salt to taste, and lemon juice. Mix well to coat the chicken evenly. Cover the bowl and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for best flavor.

instructions.title: Cook the Chicken
instructions.text: Heat 1 tablespoon of butter in a large pan or skillet over medium-high heat. Add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, working in batches if necessary to avoid overcrowding. Cook for 5-7 minutes, turning occasionally, until the chicken is browned and cooked through. Remove the cooked chicken and set aside.

instructions.title: Prepare the Gravy Base
instructions.text: In the same pan, add another 2 tablespoons of butter. Once melted, add the finely chopped onion and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Add 1 tbsp ginger-garlic paste and cook for another minute until fragrant. Stir in the crushed tomatoes, 1 tsp cumin powder, 1 tsp coriander powder, and 1 tsp red chili powder. Cook for 10-12 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes break down and the mixture thickens, and oil starts to separate from the sides.

instructions.title: Blend the Gravy (Optional)
instructions.text: For a smoother, restaurant-style gravy, carefully transfer the cooked tomato mixture to a blender or use an immersion blender. Blend until completely smooth. Strain the gravy through a fine-mesh sieve back into the pan for an even silkier texture. This step is optional but highly recommended for the classic Murgh Makhani consistency.

instructions.title: Simmer with Chicken
instructions.text: Return the smooth gravy to the pan over medium heat. Add the cooked chicken pieces to the gravy. Stir gently to combine. Add 1-2 teaspoons of sugar or honey to balance the tanginess of the tomatoes. Bring the mixture to a gentle simmer and cook for 5-7 minutes, allowing the flavors to meld and the chicken to absorb the gravy.

instructions.title: Finish and Garnish
instructions.text: Stir in the heavy cream, 1 tablespoon of crushed Kasuri Methi, and the remaining 1 tablespoon of butter. Cook for another 2-3 minutes, just until heated through; do not boil after adding cream. Taste and adjust seasoning if needed. Garnish with fresh chopped cilantro before serving.

tips: For a richer, deeper flavor, consider adding a paste of 10-12 soaked cashews or almonds to the gravy along with the cream. This also helps thicken the sauce naturally.
Always crush Kasuri Methi (dried fenugreek leaves) between your palms before adding to the curry to release its full aromatic potential. It is a key flavor component in authentic Butter Chicken.
Do not boil the curry vigorously after adding the cream, as it can curdle. Gently simmer on low heat until just heated through for a smooth, creamy finish.
article:
Butter Chicken Classic Murgh Makhani: Your Guide to a Beloved Indian Dish

Few dishes capture the heart and palate quite like Butter Chicken, known in Hindi as Murgh Makhani. This iconic Indian curry is a global sensation, celebrated for its rich, creamy texture, tantalizing aroma, and perfectly cooked chicken. It's a dish that evokes comfort, warmth, and the vibrant flavors of Indian cuisine. Whether you're a seasoned chef or a home cook eager to explore new culinary horizons, mastering classic Butter Chicken is a rewarding experience. This comprehensive guide will walk you through everything you need to know to create an authentic and unforgettable Murgh Makhani right in your own kitchen.

## What is Butter Chicken (Murgh Makhani)?

Butter Chicken, or Murgh Makhani, translates literally to "chicken with butter." Its origins trace back to the 1950s in Delhi, India, at the Moti Mahal restaurant. The story goes that leftover tandoori chicken was combined with a rich tomato-based gravy, butter, and cream to prevent it from drying out. The result was a culinary masterpiece that quickly gained popularity, becoming a staple in Indian restaurants worldwide.

At its core, Murgh Makhani features tender pieces of chicken (traditionally tandoori chicken, but pan-fried or baked works beautifully) swimming in a luxurious, mildly spiced tomato and cashew-based gravy. The defining characteristics are its velvety smoothness, a subtle tang from tomatoes, a hint of sweetness, and a generous amount of butter and cream that contribute to its signature richness. It’s a dish that perfectly balances savory, tangy, and sweet notes, making it incredibly appealing to a wide range of palates.

## Ingredients for Classic Butter Chicken

Crafting the perfect Butter Chicken requires a careful selection of fresh ingredients. Here's what you'll need:

**For the Chicken Marinade:**
*   500g boneless, skinless chicken thighs or breasts, cut into 1-inch pieces
*   1/2 cup plain yogurt
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 teaspoon red chili powder (Kashmiri chili powder for color, or regular for heat)
*   1/2 teaspoon turmeric powder
*   1 teaspoon garam masala
*   1/2 teaspoon salt
*   1 tablespoon lemon juice

**For the Makhani Gravy:**
*   2 tablespoons unsalted butter, plus more for finishing
*   1 large onion, roughly chopped
*   1 tablespoon ginger-garlic paste
*   1 green chili (optional, for heat)
*   1 cup canned crushed tomatoes (or 3-4 fresh ripe tomatoes, roughly chopped)
*   1/2 cup cashews (soaked in hot water for 15-20 minutes, then drained)
*   1/2 cup water or chicken broth
*   Whole spices: 2-3 green cardamom pods, 1-inch cinnamon stick, 2-3 cloves, 1 bay leaf
*   Powdered spices: 1 teaspoon coriander powder, 1/2 teaspoon cumin powder, 1 teaspoon red chili powder, 1/2 teaspoon garam masala
*   1 tablespoon kasoori methi (dried fenugreek leaves), crushed
*   1/2 cup heavy cream, plus more for garnish
*   1-2 teaspoons sugar (to balance acidity, adjust to taste)
*   Salt to taste

**For Garnish:**
*   Fresh cilantro, chopped
*   A swirl of fresh cream

## How to Make Butter Chicken: Step-by-Step

Creating this beloved dish is a journey of flavors, and here's how to embark on it:

**Step 1: Marinate the Chicken**
In a large bowl, combine the chicken pieces with all the marinade ingredients. Mix well to ensure every piece is coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 30 minutes, or preferably 2-4 hours for maximum flavor absorption.

**Step 2: Cook the Chicken**
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil or butter in a large pan or cast-iron skillet over medium-high heat. Once hot, add the marinated chicken pieces in a single layer, ensuring not to overcrowd the pan. Cook until the chicken is lightly charred and cooked through, about 5-7 minutes per side. You can also grill or bake the chicken at 400°F (200°C) for 15-20 minutes until cooked. Set the cooked chicken aside.

**Step 3: Prepare the Makhani Gravy Base**
In the same pan (or a clean pot), melt 2 tablespoons of butter over medium heat. Add the whole spices (cardamom, cinnamon, cloves, bay leaf) and sauté for 30 seconds until fragrant. Add the chopped onions and cook until softened and translucent, about 5-7 minutes. Stir in the ginger-garlic paste and green chili (if using), cooking for another minute until aromatic.

**Step 4: Build the Gravy Flavors**
Add the crushed tomatoes and the soaked cashews to the pan. Cook for 8-10 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the tomatoes soften and the mixture thickens slightly. Add 1/2 cup of water or chicken broth, bring to a simmer, then remove from heat.

**Step 5: Blend the Gravy**
Carefully transfer the gravy mixture to a blender. Remove the bay leaf before blending, if desired. Blend until completely smooth and creamy. This step is crucial for the signature silky texture of Murgh Makhani.

**Step 6: Finish the Gravy**
Return the blended gravy to the pot. For an extra smooth finish, you can strain the gravy through a fine-mesh sieve, pressing down on any solids. Bring the gravy to a gentle simmer over medium-low heat. Stir in the powdered spices (coriander, cumin, red chili powder, garam masala) and kasoori methi. Cook for 5 minutes, allowing the spices to meld. Add the cooked chicken pieces to the gravy.

**Step 7: Add the Cream and Final Touches**
Stir in the heavy cream and a knob of butter. Add sugar to taste – this helps balance the acidity of the tomatoes. Season with salt as needed. Simmer for another 5-7 minutes, allowing the chicken to absorb the rich flavors of the gravy. Do not boil vigorously after adding cream, as it can curdle.

**Step 8: Garnish and Serve**
Remove from heat. Garnish generously with fresh chopped cilantro and a swirl of fresh cream. Your homemade classic Butter Chicken is ready!

## Pro Tips for the Best Murgh Makhani

Achieving restaurant-quality Butter Chicken at home is entirely possible with a few expert tips:

*   **Marination is Key:** Don't skimp on marination time. The longer the chicken marinates, the more tender and flavorful it will be. Overnight is ideal.
*   **Charred Chicken:** For an authentic tandoori flavor, cook the chicken until it has a slight char. A grill, cast-iron skillet, or even a broiler works wonders.
*   **Silky Smooth Gravy:** Blend the gravy base thoroughly until there are no visible chunks. Straining it through a fine-mesh sieve after blending will give you an incredibly smooth, restaurant-quality texture.
*   **Kasoori Methi:** This dried fenugreek leaf is a non-negotiable ingredient. Crush it between your palms before adding it to the gravy to release its unique, slightly bitter, aromatic flavor. It's what gives Butter Chicken its distinctive taste.
*   **Balance of Flavors:** Taste and adjust. The perfect Murgh Makhani has a balance of sweet, tangy, and savory. Don't hesitate to add a little more sugar if your tomatoes are very acidic, or a pinch more salt.
*   **Good Quality Butter and Cream:** Since these are central to the dish, investing in good quality unsalted butter and full-fat heavy cream will make a noticeable difference in richness and flavor.

## Serving Suggestions for Butter Chicken

Butter Chicken is a versatile dish that pairs wonderfully with a variety of accompaniments. For a classic Indian meal, serve it with:

*   **Naan Bread:** Warm, fluffy naan (plain, garlic, or butter naan) is perfect for scooping up every last drop of the rich gravy.
*   **Basmati Rice:** Steamed basmati rice or fragrant jeera rice (cumin rice) provides a lovely contrast and helps soak up the sauce.
*   **Raita:** A cooling yogurt-based side dish, like cucumber raita, offers a refreshing counterpoint to the richness of the curry.
*   **Simple Salad:** A light green salad with a lemon dressing can add freshness to the meal.

## Variations and Substitutions

While the classic Butter Chicken recipe is a timeless favorite, there are ways to adapt it to dietary needs or personal preferences:

*   **Vegetarian/Vegan:** Replace chicken with paneer (Indian cottage cheese), tofu, chickpeas, or mixed vegetables for a delicious vegetarian or vegan Murgh Makhani. Use plant-based butter and cream for a vegan version.
*   **Spiciness Level:** Adjust the amount of red chili powder and green chilies to control the heat. For a milder version, omit the green chili entirely and use only Kashmiri chili powder for color.
*   **Smoky Flavor:** If you don't have a tandoor, you can impart a smoky flavor (dhungar method) by placing a small, hot piece of charcoal in a small bowl within the gravy, drizzling a teaspoon of oil or ghee over it, and quickly covering the pot for a few minutes.
*   **Healthier Twist:** Reduce the amount of butter and cream, or use low-fat cream alternatives. While it won't be as rich, it can still be flavorful.

Butter Chicken is more than just a meal; it's an experience. Its creamy texture, aromatic spices, and tender chicken make it a dish that delights senses and creates lasting memories. By following this guide, you're well on your way to mastering this beloved Indian classic and bringing the authentic taste of Murgh Makhani to your table. Enjoy the process, savor the flavors, and share this incredible culinary creation with your loved ones.
